subject: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)

Team —

As we prep QBR content next week I pulled a short "service debt" snapshot focused on items that are materially affecting SLA attainment for Hosted API customers. I attached a CSV with the candidate list and a short PDF with proposed slides/asks. High-level points: 

- SLA variance: three models across two regions have persistent 95th pct latency drift vs target (eu-west and us-west).
- Recent customer-impacting incidents: two degradations in token-serving pipeline (20270503 & 20270508) tied to metadata cache eviction and a fallback routing regression.
- OKR alignment: infra reliability OKRs are behind on MTTR and roll-forward items; we need a narrower exec ask list for the QBR.

Requesting: quick takes from engineering leads by 10:30 PT today so I can consolidate for the exec packet:
  1) Root cause summary + mitigation status for the two incidents (one-line each) — Vivek
  2) Action owners and ETA for stabilizing the 95th pct latency (narrow target: 3-week runway) — Marissa / Marcus
  3) Any CS/customer asks that should be surfaced to Acme and other accounts — Hannah

I propose the following QBR asks (draft): funded runway for a dedicated reliability sprints budget, prioritized canary for routing fallback, and customer credits for impacted tenants if we miss the next SLA check-window.

Attachments: service-debt-candidate-list.csv (rows with incident id, service, impact), qbr-prep-notes.pdf (slide outline + ask language).

Thanks — quick pulses appreciated.

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Reliability & Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)

Sofia —

Short answers per your asks: 

1) Incidents root cause (one-liners):
   - 2027-05-03: metadata cache eviction due to load spike exposed a latent race in KV warmup; automatic fallback incorrectly routed to a higher-latency variant. Mitigation: temporary rate gate in front of cache write path deployed (PATCH-859), longer-term fix in RFC (INF-4832).
   - 2027-05-08: rollout of routing policy change caused weight calculation to favor a new variant with untested quantized kernels; rollback completed within 42m. Mitigation: revert + added rollout canary gate (ROLL-23).

2) Stabilizing 95th pct: short plan
   - Week 1: lock routing policy and add stricter canary thresholds (owner: Marissa)
   - Week 2: KV warmup improvements + prewarm instrumentation (owner: Marcus)
   - Week 3: targeted QOS tuning on affected GPU pools (owner: Infra Ops)

I support an exec ask for a 4-week funded reliability sprint budget to ensure dedicated engineers can execute the above without context switching. If we commit to crediting impacted customers, propose a uniform credit policy (0.5% of monthly usage for affected window) — that will land well with Acme.

Vivek
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)

+1 to Vivek's plan. A couple of operational clarifications: 

- Canary cadence: we'll run a 2-hour canary window for any routing policy change before global rollout. Ops runbook will include an explicit failover test and rollback timer. (Marcus to own the canary dashboard updates.)
- Dependencies: INF-4832 (KV warmup) needs cross-team help from model-onboarding to validate cache priming for new model variants — I added owners in the ticket.
- ETA: I can commit to Week 1 gating and a Week 2 rollout of prewarm changes (slated for 2027-05-24).

Action owners I'll surface in the QBR slide: Marissa (policy gating), Marcus (prewarm + canary dashboard), Vivek (sprint budget ask).

Marissa
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Green <sam.green@acme-analytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)

Sofia / Team —

Thanks for the crisp summary. From Acme's side the two incidents caused measurable downstream query latency for our pipelines on 5/3 and 5/8 which pushed back a customer deliverable. We appreciate the proposed credit and the canary plan. Two requests: 

1) Can you share a short technical postmortem we can attach to our internal incident tracker? A one-page summary with timeline and mitigations is enough.
2) For the QBR, can you include a proposed SLA remediation timeline so our procurement team can plan contingencies?

If helpful, Jill (copied) from VendorOps can coordinate acceptance testing for the routing canary on our end.

Sam Green
Head of ML Platform
Acme Analytics
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@acme-analytics.com>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@vendorops.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service debt snapshot + QBR asks (SLAs, incidents, OKR alignment)

Thanks all — quick consolidation and next steps below (for the exec packet):

1) Postmortem deliverable: one-page timeline + mitigation list. Owner: Vivek. Delivery: 2027-05-13 EOD. (Will share a draft in the Drive link.)
2) SLA remediation timeline: three-week runway with weekly checkpoints. Owner: Marissa / Marcus. Deliverable: concise timeline slide for QBR (due 2027-05-18).
3) Canary & acceptance testing: Marcus to update dashboard; Acme/VendorOps to join canary acceptance window. Scheduled tentative window: 2027-05-20 09:00-11:00 PT.
4) Exec asks (finalize): 4-week funded reliability sprint + temporary credits policy for affected customers. Owner for ask language: Sofia (I will finalize slides).

I will fold these into qbr-prep-notes.pdf and circulate an exec packet tomorrow morning. If anyone wants to escalate a different ask to the GTM leadership (discounts vs credits vs extended support), ping me directly — we'll keep the exec ask narrow.

Sofia
Director, Reliability & Platform
Redwood Inference
